utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before we continue with the witness, we shall have a Status Conference just to deal with one or two matters. The Trial Chamber has observed that the filings of the parties on depositions have not complied with what has been agreed all along. I wish to remind the parties to look at the -- the Defence, rather, to look at the confidential joint Defence motion dated 14th November last year, and also the Defence submissions of 29th November, 2003, during the proceedings. The deposition evidence is intended to be brief and to be limited to one or two incidents only. The timing listed by the parties was way out of what was agreed upon in the submissions I've referred to. The Trial Chamber has, therefore, decided to limit the time for the witnesses who are going to give depositions for both parties so that examination-in-chief will be for 40 minutes, cross-examination, if any, will be 25 minutes, and re-examination, if required, will be for 15 minutes for each deponent. Each accused has seven deponents in this matter. That's all. The Trial Chamber has also been informed that the Defence for Mr. Blagoje Simic, Mr. Pantelic, has not submitted the summary for the witnesses they intend to submit to the Prosecution. That's why the Prosecution has not been able to make their status known to the Trial Chamber. Mr. Pantelic, this matter has been pending for some time. Can you submit summaries to both the Prosecution and the Trial Chamber by 1300 hours on Monday?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was informed yesterday by the court officer, and I just filed it ten minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So one copy is for the Prosecution, the other for the Trial Chamber. As I stated in my submission on 29th of November, Ms. Andric was the bank officer in Samac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That is sufficient. We shall see the summaries. You have already spoken about the witness. The Trial Chamber has also been informed that Mr. Lukic, I think, is -- has some Rule 92 submissions -- statements for submissions. We shall now close the Status Conference and move into the proceedings. Mr. Lukic, you can go ahead before the witness comes in, if you are ready, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do apologise. Just -- it's issue for the technical booth. We have a problem with our laptop. So in the meantime, if someone can come, the Defence would appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, yes. The Defence of Miroslav Tadic got the official translations of a certain number of 92 bis statements. However, in relation to depositions, I would just kindly ask the Trial Chamber for an explanation. Since depositions are limited to certain facts and certain events, as you said yourself, will the Trial Chamber take the following position: Is the cross-examination strictly linked to what the examination-in-chief is about? Because it would really be a problem for us if the cross-examination would deal with some other issues, those that were not raised during the examination-in-chief. I think it would be important for both parties to be aware of the position of the Trial Chamber, especially in view of the fact that you have just restricted our time for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It is not exactly correct to say the time has been restricted by the Trial Chamber because these matters were discussed and the submission is there from the parties. Yes. The cross-examination, of course, will have to be limited to 15 minutes, but the Trial Chamber cannot limit the Prosecution as to where or what issues they will raise, because they're entitled to do that under the Rules. So we cannot change the Rules. It's just the time limitation. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours, please, I assume it was a slip of the tongue when you said 15 minutes for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Yes, it's 25 minutes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I appreciate your interpretation, and I just wanted to tell the Trial Chamber one more thing. On behalf of the Defence teams, I sent the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina a letter, the government of the federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, namely the committee for cooperation with The Hague Tribunal that has to do with the demography expertise, and I hope that we are going to get a response for them in due time. However, if I do not get an answer in good time, then I'm going to notify the Trial Chamber thereof, so then perhaps we'll have to do something with the deadlines. We are now prepared to introduce the following 92 bis statements. Could we please move into private session now for a minute or two because of the first statement? I need to say something in private session about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, we'll move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next statement I wish to introduce is the statement of Witness Milka Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The previous exhibit will be under seal to safeguard the interest of the witness until further decision by the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The statement of Mr. Milka Petkovic will be treated as D115/3 ID, and D115/3 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next statement that the Defence of Miroslav Tadic wishes to tender is the statement of Witness Zeljko Volasevic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This statement will be treated as D116/3 ID, and D116/3 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next statement we would like to tender into evidence is the statement of witness Stanko Bojic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This statement will be treated as D117/3 ID, and D117/3 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next statement we wish to tender into evidence is the statement of witness Hasan Pistoljevic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This statement will be treated as D118/3 ID and D118/3 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next statement that we wish to tender into evidence is the statement taken according to Rule 92 bis for witness Djordje Dujkovic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This statement will be treated as D119/3 ID and D119/3 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next statement is the statement of witness Ilija Mihalj. I repeat the name for the interpreters. Ilija Mihalj.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note that the court reporters will get the spelling correctly eventually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This statement will be treated as D120/3 ID and D120/3 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next statement that I wish to tender into evidence is the statement of witness Marko Kuresevic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This statement will be treated as D121/3 ID and D121/3 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next statement is the statement of witness Muhamed Atic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This statement will be treated as D122/3 ID and D122/3 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the last statement that we wish to tender into evidence this time is the statement of witness Abdulah Arslanovic. In accordance with the decision of the Trial Chamber, the Defence of Miroslav Tadic is supposed to tender three more witness statements, and we shall do our best to abide by the instructions given by the Trial Chamber. Namely, we shall submit them in the month of February.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This statement will be treated as D123/3 ID and D123/3 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: For these statements that have been submitted today, the Trial Chamber has given the Prosecution six working days to indicate their status, whether they wish to cross-examine the witness. That is by Friday next week, 1300 hours. We now proceed with our witness. Mr. Pisarevic, you are still cross-examining when the witness comes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Pisarevic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, Mr. Vukovic. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, we talked about your listening to Mr. Zaric speak on the radio sometime in February or March. The next question which I wish to ask you stems from the fact that in your statement, you referred to an evacuation of women and children on May 16th and 17th, 1992, and you said that the evacuation had been organised by the command of the brigade from Samac. Can you respond for the Trial Chamber on the basis of what did you obtain that knowledge? Did you see any decision of that command, any list drawn up by that command in connection with that evacuation?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Immediately, the first break, I told these ladies who were there who were preparing me, I told him that I had made a mistake when I said that the military command had been compiling these lists. What I meant to say was that the lists were made in the Red Cross, but the military command had submitted information about the families of the fighters who were on the front line, and it asked for those families if possible to be given priority vis-a-vis the other citizens because the fighters were engaged at the front line. I also said that as far as the Civil Defence staff was concerned, our task, our job, was only to provide the bus. So I made this mistake. I made -- I mentioned them in the context of data, because the Red Cross couldn't draw up this list if it didn't have information from the command as to which families these were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If I understood you correctly, you are now testifying here that the -- that the command, when it came to the list submitted the lists of women and children, the families of its own members, to the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All the lists were actually drawn up in the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the fact that as a citizen of Samac you had lived in Samac for so many years, until -- also until the outbreak of the hostilities on the 17th of April, 1992, and that you remained there throughout the period of the war operations, were you in a position to see any members of the police as of the 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me -- or, rather, can you tell the Trial Chamber, did you notice, did you observe any difference in the uniforms worn by the police until the 17th of April, 1992, and the uniforms which they wore after or as of the 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a considerable difference in their uniforms. Until the 17th of April, they wore the classical blue uniforms with the caps that were police caps, standard regulation caps. And after the hostilities, the war, broke out, they put berets on their heads, and they wore camouflage uniforms, black and blue camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did their [Realtime transcript read in error "hero"] head of [as interpreted] Stevan Todorovic also wear such a uniform?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I just have another question before completing my questioning. You have lived in Samac for a long time --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's on page 10, line 5. Mr. Pisarevic didn't say did their hero Stevan Todorovic, did their chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I don't think it would make much difference.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note the interpreters said head, head of police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You lived in Samac, if I understood you correctly for a long time, and if I heard you correctly you had known Simo Zaric for a long time. Could you just describe in one sentence for the Trial Chamber the person of Simo Zaric, his status, the reputation he enjoyed among the citizens of Samac, the city of Samac, the municipality of Samac, and anything else that you might know on that score.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have known Simo Zaric for many years. I don't know whether these are the beginnings, whether it was the beginnings of his career when we worked together in a company, but later he became head of a transport group in the Bosanka trading company. So we worked together for a year or two, I'm not quite certain, and he was later transferred. He later moved to SUP to work. He stayed in the SUP for a while, and then -- then found employment with the work organisation enterprise called -- called Buducnost to the company in Belgrade, and then he came to Belgrade, worked for the state security in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We know all that.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We saw each other. We were often together. Sometimes I would organise some little get-togethers in my house, and that couldn't go past without Simo Zaric. My family liked Simo Zaric, is very fond of him. And not only my family but an overwhelming number of the population in Samac municipality is -- are very fond of Simo. You know, people are popular if they can sing and dance and be congenial in the company of others, and Simo Zaric is precisely that kind of a man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Cross-examination, Mr. Weiner. Cross-examined by Mr. Weiner:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Vukovic.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My name is Philip Weiner. I'm a Prosecutor here with the Office of the Prosecution and I've got some questions to ask you today. Could the witness be shown Exhibit D110/3, please. Do you remember looking at that exhibit yesterday, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You can sit down Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And having looked at that, would you agree with me that the title of that is "List of civilians from Samac municipality who have been killed"?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that that list, sir, is inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It is an accurate list, and I knew more than half of the people on this list personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's -- let's look at it. Your friend who you talked about yesterday whose nickname was Antesa, Anto Brandic, could you please show me where his name appears on that list, the same Anto Brandic, or Antesa, that was murdered by Stevan Todorovic? Could you please look at the list to your right, sir, and show me where his name appears.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry. The interpreter did not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can the witness repeat what he said? The interpreters didn't hear it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Repeat. I cannot find Brandic on this list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, there was another man with the exact same name, Anto Brandic, whose nickname was Dikan who we've had a lot of testimony in this case, and it's not being contested by these Defence counsel, that was murdered at the Territorial Defence building by Lugar, having been shot in the head in April of 1992. Obviously his name isn't on that list either, is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know Dikan. I never heard of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But his name is not on that list. There is no second Anto Brandic nicknamed Dikan on that list either?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't found any Anto Brandic. I don't know what serial number. If you can tell me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't have a serial number. I have his name and nickname. But I know it does not appear on that list, sir. Sir, isn't it also true that the names Bato Kljajic, and Marko Evic. The Bato last name is K-L-J-A-J-I-C, and Marko Evic, who were both shot to death at the secondary school by Lugar on the 7th of July, 1992. Those names do not appear on that list.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about these two men, that they were killed, but yesterday in my statement I said everything that all the people who were actually killed in prisons in Samac, in SUP, in the school, as regards all those, we were neither informed nor did we organise their funerals. They were not taken to the morgue, and we in the civil and defence staff therefore did not know about those people who were killed in prison. This was the concern of the organs of the SUP. Where they were buried and when and who had been killed, we didn't know. I heard -- I said yesterday that I only heard in The Hague about Antesa, and I'm very sorry this should have happened to him as a human being. That was not accessible to the public. Such knowledge was not accessible to the public.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, my question is did those two names appear on -- that those two names do not appear on that list. Is that correct? Would you agree with me that those two names, Bato Kljajic and Marko Evic do not appear on that list?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, are you aware that also in 1992, in the summer, Dr. Ruza Brdar Masic, do you know Dr. Ruza Brdar Masic? Dr. Ruza from Samac?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Yes, I know her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, are you aware that she was also called to the high school to pronounce a man dead, an elderly man from Vidovici or Kanapici, and there is no indication of any elderly man from Kanapici or Vidovici who was beaten to death on that list? Would you agree with me? There is no indication of anyone that was beaten to death on that list? So that one was also not listed.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I have no knowledge that Dr. Ruza was called to the SUP or to the prison. We had no connection whatsoever with the prison, we from the civil defence staff. I never even peeked in there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question, sir, is there any indication on that list of a person being beaten to death, elderly man from one of those two towns, Vidovici or Kanapici? Would you take my word for it there is no such indication on that list? Or you can look at it yourself?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know Vidovici and Kanapici, and I've never heard of them, so I can't say anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there is no indication on that list where it says place of residence Vidovici or Kanapici? There is no indication on that list. If you want to look at it, it's three pages. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nor is there any indication on that list of an elderly man who has been beaten to death in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I am objecting to the line of questioning. The witness has stated repeatedly what he knows about these people. And now the question is whether they were beaten to death. And the witness has said that he doesn't know anything about that and he has repeatedly said he doesn't know with precision.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's not my question. My question is, if you look at the list it has how these people were killed, where these people were from. It has an approximate age, it has the year of birth. I'm asking if specific people who were murdered in Bosanski Samac, civilians, are listed on that list, and that's all I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It's a question of the witness looking at the document in front of him and answering the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Omer -- Fikret Omeragic is the first man from Samac who is on this list, and the first shelling on Samac hit Fikret and he succumbed to his wounds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, that's not my question. My question is: Is there any indication on that list of an elderly man who was beaten to death in Samac?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see on this list, this is all shells, shells, bullets. There is Ilija Antunic from Grebnice killed in the HVO, and Vojo Micic from Domaljevac killed in the HVO. The rest is from shells and wounds and bullets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. There is no person indicated on that list that was beaten to death. Let us continue. We've had testimony about a man Aladin Jakupovic. His nickname was Dadi. Did you know him, sir, Aladin Jakupovic? He was a large man, a bouncer or a doorman at a club or cafe.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I hear of this person. I don't know him, and I've never seen him. Perhaps I've seen him, but I don't know the man. I've never -- I don't know about any Jakupovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was murdered in April or May of 1992 by a group of the Serbian volunteers. Do you see his name on that list, Aladin Jakupovic, nicknamed Dadi, or would you agree with me it does not appear on that list?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not find that first and last name on this list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, we've had testimony about another man nicknamed Suma from Bosanski Samac. His name is Rusmir Hodzic nicknamed Suma. Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was beaten to death at the Territorial Defence building. He was severely beaten, but he died in July -- I'm sorry, June or July of 1992 at the hospital in Bosanski Samac as a result of those beatings. Do you see his name on the list, Suma nickname, Rusmir Hodzic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said also in my statement yesterday, and I've said now and I'm repeating, that everything which happened in prison as to who was beaten, who was killed, I have no connection with that whatsoever, nor do I know anything about that. And I cannot say anything about it, and I cannot speak about things that I know nothing about it. I just want to tell the truth, and I cannot say anything about things that I know nothing about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, the question is: Does the name appear on the list or do you agree with me that his name is not on the list? That's all I'm asking. I'm not blaming you for those deaths or indicating that you're responsible in any way for those deaths. I'm just asking does that name appear on that list.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please bear with me. I've gone through the his for -- several times looking for the names and surnames of these people that you're asking. You're asking about this person, and you know that he is not on the list. Why are you making me re-read the list to look for the first and last name of a man with whom I have no connection whatsoever, and you know that he is not on the list and it is not on the list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that name is not on the list. What about the 16 people who were killed in Crkvina, the 16 non-Serb civilians, and I believe you probably have known some of them such as Jozo Bosalic. None of their names appear on that list. Nine locals and seven from Teslic. There is no indication on this list of anyone from Teslic that was -- any civilian from Teslic that was murdered, and none of those other nine names, Jozo Antunovic, Luka Gregurevic, such as Niko Brandic, Ilija Matic, Ivo Tuzla, just to name a few, none of those names appear on this list, sir. So since these 16 names don't appear on the list and those others that we have, you must agree with me, sir, this is not an accurate list of the civilians that were killed in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object to this question because the witness should be asked to clarify what civilians are, whether detained persons are civilians, and only then whether he accepts this contention of the Prosecution without going into the legal terminology in which the witness is not versed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, asking him what a civilian is is a legal issue. We've had a lot of testimony in this case as to the civilians who were illegally detained that were not notified of any charges, and that's our argument, that these were civilians. Some of these people were isolated, the people in the high school. We've had testimony that these people were isolated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner. Isn't the answer from the witness that of those who were isolated in prisons or wherever, he doesn't know anything about them and they don't appear on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's all I want is his answer that those people don't appear on the list. So therefore, this is an inaccurate list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I thought that his answer was complete.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I asked the question. I didn't receive an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh. All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This list which is before me is accurate according to the records which were maintained on the funerals of civilians killed in the territory of Samac municipality, killed by shells and bullets, the effects of the war operations. And as I've said, those who were killed in the prison in Crkvina, that is something that we had no connection with whatsoever. Yesterday I said that I had found out about this incident in Crkvina, and I asked Miroslav Tadic about it, and he told me, unfortunately I have also heard of it, and whether it was true, he couldn't tell me. And of all these people who were killed in Crkvina, I felt the most sorry for a person, the last name of whom the interpreter couldn't catch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the person, the last name? Sir, what was the name of the person you felt most sorry for?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Josip Orsolic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that he had been among the people who had been killed at Crkvina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then, sir, if those people, those civilians who were murdered in Samac, those Muslim and Croat civilians who were murdered, who you didn't bury but were murdered in Samac, their names do not appear on this list, then this is not an accurate list of those people killed in Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object. This is a repetition of the same question as awhile ago. Now the -- is the -- the Prosecutor is imputing to this witness that these were civilians, and the witness said these were detainees and these are wholly different categories. The witness explained very clearly and very precisely that these were civilians killed in the city from the effects of shelling. So this is a totally different category. And the Prosecutor is trying to impose this on the witness while the witness has no factual knowledge or legal knowledge to actually make the distinction between civilians, prisoners of war, and detainees. I believe that this calls for a legal conclusion on the part of the witness through the way the question has been posed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness hasn't answered the question. It does not call for a legal conclusion. It calls for a very simple conclusion. If you have a group of people who are not on the list --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, what Mr. Lukic was talking about is your classifications of civilians. If you simply say persons, I think that will stop the problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if those persons, names, are not on this list, then you would agree with me that this is not a complete list of the persons in Bosanski Samac that were killed?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that this was -- is the complete list made on the basis of records of killed civilians in the territory of Bosanski Samac from bullets, shells, and mines. And I also clearly indicated -- said that what happened in prison was the concern of the bodies of the secretariat of internal affairs which did not inform us --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not my question. Listen to my question carefully?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, can you move on? I think the answers are sufficient at this point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, yesterday you testified about the illegal arming of local people in Samac by political parties. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your testimony, you did not mention the arming of locals by the SDS political party; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that the SDS party was illegally arming its members?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you testified early today about your friend Simo Zaric, your long friend. Your friend Simo Zaric, who you've been friends with for a very long time; correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that 1998, Simo Zaric gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor where he describes the illegal arming in Bosanski Samac by the SDS party?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of any reason why Simo Zaric would say that the SDS party was illegally arming its members if it wasn't true?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether Simo knew whether there was arming going on or not, but I didn't know about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you're aware that your old friend Simo Zaric was involved in intelligence work and had worked for state security, so-called secret police?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't call it the secret police. It wasn't the secret police while Simo worked at the state security service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that state security service, he was involved in intelligence.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not know what work he -- what work he was engaged in at the state security service. This was not accessible to us civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did you ever provide any information to Simo Zaric at the SDB or the state security service?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no information to give him. I don't know. I don't know what kind of information he may have been interested in. The kind of information that I could provide him with. While he worked at the state security service, he and I never, ever talked about work. I did things that were completely different from the work that he did at the state security service. So we had nothing to talk about in that respect ever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, sir, he has testified here -- or not testified, he's provided a statement indicating that the SDS was illegally arming its members, the Serbian SDS. Do you know of any reason why he would say that if it wasn't true?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I finally have to object to this line. How could a witness possibly know why Mr. Zaric said something in his statement. This is direct calling for speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's a common question on the issue bias. He could say, well Simo is a liar; he could say Simo is not truthful; he can say Simo has mental problems and just makes things up; he can say Simo's honest man.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I followed the question. It's properly put to the witness and the witness can answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot say what Simo stated, how he stated it, what he knew and what I did not know about. I did not know that SDS was arming people. If Simo Zaric knew about that and I don't know whether he knew about that, I mean, I cannot give a different answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is: Do you know of any reason why he would say it if it wasn't true? Knowing Simo Zaric as you do, do you know of any reason why he would say it if it wasn't true? I'm not asking you whether or not you were aware of the arming. Do you know of any reason why he would make that statement that the SDS was arming its members if it wasn't true?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not answer that question. I don't know the answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on. Sir, you were working at the pensioners' building for approximately a year, 1992, 1993.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And each morning in 1992 when you got there, did you see a large group of people standing out front of the pensioners' home awaiting their work assignments?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you know any of these people? Did you recognise any Muslim or Croat friends, acquaintances, neighbours standing in that line or in that group?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And those people were waiting to receive their work assignments or work orders from Beg Kapetanovic, as you testified yesterday, and then you said a Celic, is that Dzevad Celic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And those people would give out those work assignments. Now, were you aware that some of those Muslim and Croat civilians, as part of their work assignments, were being sent to the front lines to dig trenches and to construct bunkers for the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not know where they went and what kind of work they did and who engaged them. I knew that they were going out for their work assignments, for their work obligation, and what work they actually did is something that I did not know, and I and the rest of us at the civilian protection staff were not interested in this. That was not our affair.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you ever learn, as part of your -- as part of your work, that two young men were killed in crossfire while digging trenches at the front lines and they're on that list we had in front you previously, number 41, Dzevad Drigic, son of Galib, and number 75, Redzep Idriza [phoen], son of Muharem. Were you aware of that, those two young men on that list that you just had in front of you a little while ago -- list of civilians killed during the war, that they were killed while digging trenches on the front lines as part of their work?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you also testified yesterday about certain types of work and assignments. Are you all right? Are you okay?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Sorry. You also testified yesterday about certain work assignments that were given and that came through your office, and you mentioned various assignments that were sent down to Beg Kapetanovic and Celic, requests for work. Now, let's talk about another area you talked about. You talked about repairing of glass. Do you remember that yesterday? Broken windows, glass.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you talked about and you discussed how it was a major problem in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you mentioned that you used the glass from the Uniglas, and you used so much glass that you went through their whole inventory of glass.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if we went through their whole inventory, but the next time we were supposed to glaze some windows there was no glass left. The first time when windows were broken in town, they did send us glass, but the next time there was no glass for it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you repair these windows with this stock, glass stock, it's not -- there's a number of different tasks that have to be done such as removing the broken glass, measuring the glass, checking the frame to see if it's bent, placing the -- cutting the glass, placing the piece of glass in there, and you need someone with some basic carpentry or glazier -- glass work as background. You didn't do that work, did you, sir?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this cannot be done by people who don't know how to work with glass and who don't have the right things to work with. I think it was Kapetanovic who was there then, and we asked him for men who had tools to cut glass with and who knew how to do that kind of work, and they were then engaged for this work by their superiors who assigned them to do that. They were made available to the civilian protection staff until the glazing business was finished.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I just want to say that basically you and Miroslav Tadic didn't do that yourselves, but you went downstairs to Beg Kapetanovic and Dzevad Celic to get the workers to do it; correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said yesterday that it was not our job to take workers and to assign them to what they were supposed to do. We always had to ask them. They were under the Ministry of Defence, and we had those people downstairs who were actually handing out the assignments. And then when we, the civilian protection staff, were supposed to carry out work that we were in charge of, then we said to them exactly what kind of people we needed. I mentioned the people who made coffins. Yesterday I mentioned them. A coffin could not be made by someone who doesn't know how to make a coffin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What we're talking about is the glass. So what you would do is when you had the jobs, you would notify Beg Kapetanovic and Dzevad Celic, and they would supply the labour; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you know a man by the name of Teufik Drljacic? He was a local glazier, a window man. Halid Drljacic his brother. Did you know him or hear of him?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was he one of the men who was out there repairing glass and windows and things?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not say, and I'll tell you why. We at the civilian protection staff, as far as this group of construction workers were concerned for repairing glass, windows, buildings, et cetera, this was led by Ismet Ramusovic. I really had nothing to do with people who were engaged in that particular line of work, but I know how this was done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on that type of repairing, in addition to the glass and that type of repairing of buildings and other matters, you would also go down to Beg Kapetanovic. So if a roof had to be repaired or a door had to be repaired, you would go to Beg Kapetanovic or Dzevad Celic and ask for people with those specialties to do that work. Is that correct? You and Ismet Ramusovic, your co-worker?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. Sir, I'd just like to talk very briefly about the mobilisation that you had observed or you had heard about that, they tried to mobilise a group of Muslims and Croats sometime, I believe, during the summer of -- based on testimony, it would have been the late summer of 1992.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday that they were asked to attend a meeting at the memorial centre. Now, why they were invited is something that I don't know, but I know that this meeting did not take place, that there was not a successful discussion, and immediately that night people started fleeing from Samac. Who invited them and for what reason is something that I don't know about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, isn't it true that after that meeting which you indicated yesterday that they were asked to take up arms that you said a number of people fled, including your son-in-law who was Croatian, and his brother? Is that true? That's what you testified to yesterday.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not what I said yesterday. I did not say that they were asked to take up arms, and my son-in-law was not Croatian but Muslim. And it's my former son-in-law at that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your former son-in-law. But did your former son-in-law and his brother flee right after that meeting?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if they fled immediately after the meeting, but they did flee that night after the meeting. The next day, they were not in Samac. At what time they fled from Samac and how is something that I would not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, after they -- after he fled, your son-in-law, was your daughter sent to Zasavica? A lot of other people whose sons, wives, husbands fled were sent to Zasavica. Was your daughter sent to Zasavica? Was she detained and sent there after her husband fled?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My daughter divorced that husband of hers in January of 1990, and nobody ever thought of war then. When the war broke out, she had nothing to do with him whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is: Was she sent to Zasavica or were you and your wife sent to Zasavica? That's all.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how come you're putting that kind of question to me. You know who was sent to Zasavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, the question is -- the question is very simple. Was your daughter-in-law -- I'm sorry. Was your daughter sent to Zasavica? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you and your wife sent to Zasavica in August of 1992?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on. You indicated that you owned some property. You owned a house. You built a house in Bosanski Samac in the area known as the first quarter or Mahala, as you described it yesterday. Maybe I'm not pronouncing it correct. The first quarter or you also called it Mahala.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fourth quarter called Mahala, the street of Vojislav Ilic, number 45.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you still live there to this day?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you live there during the war?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the first few days in the beginning, I did not, because the house was exposed to the first combat operations near the line of fire. So I didn't dare stay there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But through the rest of the war did you live there?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No one ever evicted you from that house? You never lost that house during the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's go to your sister's flat which was in the centre of the town, sir?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm sorry. One second. I asked you previously that I said no one ever evicted you from that house. You never lost that house; is that correct, and you said no. Do you mean: No, that you never lost the house, or that no, you did lose the house?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not evicted. I did not lose my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I just wanted to clarify the transcript. Now, sir, your sister's flat, did she live it in during the war, your sister?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the first few months, she had fled to Serbia. And after returning from Serbia, she went on living in that apartment where she's lived until the present day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And no one ever evicted her or forced her out of that apartment. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, your daughter, where was she living? Was she living with you or was she living with you, your sister, or did she have her own apartment or home?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My daughter stayed in the house where she had lived while she was living with that husband of hers. When they divorced, she got custody of their child, and she lived in that house throughout the war until she got married again. She remarried later again and moved to this man's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But no one ever evicted her, and she never lost the home? No?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you say no to that question and the previous one about your sister, you mean that they were never evicted. Isn't it correct that they were never evicted and they never lost their homes?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your son, where was your son living during the war? Was he living with you or --

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My son has a house of his own, and we share the same yard. During the war, he was at the front line, and his wife and child were in Serbia during the first few months. Then they returned, and they lived in Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During those months while he was at the front lines, he was away and your daughter-in-law and grandchild was away in Serbia, did anyone take that home? Did anyone move into that home?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody could have moved in because the shell had damaged it, destroyed it. Even if somebody wanted to, it wasn't possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the house eventually repaired?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And has it -- did anyone move into that home, ever move into that home or evict them from that home?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So basically no one in your family lost any property during the war through eviction or seizure.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My own nuclear family, no, but my sister who lives in the country, in a village, she had all her property destroyed. She has nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "destroyed," do you mean by shelling or did someone seize it or take custody of it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite simply it was blown up. She has nothing left, not the house itself or the facilities around the house. And units came there, units of the Croatian army, and that's where they clashed with these -- with this army of ours from Krajina, and then as they were fighting, this house was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So you agree with me that no one had any home -- had any -- no one in your family had any of their homes seized, and no one was evicted. I'm not talking about shelling, but strictly no one was evicted, no one had any of their property seized, no one lost any --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter did not hear the answer of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I just want to cover a few more areas and finish up, sir. You indicated that you didn't join the SDS party; correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're aware that that was a national party?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were aware that that was the main Serb party, sir?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. It depends on the Serbs involved. For some it was the main party and for others it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you joined the SDP party, SDP party in 1994; correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the SDP party, as opposed to the SDS party, was a multi-ethnic and more moderate party; correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the reason for your not joining the SDS, was that due to its leadership or its policies, its leadership personnel or its policies? Is that why you didn't join the SDS?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The political programmes of any political party did not suit me. I opted for the SDP because it has a programme which is a programme -- a programme which suits everyone, Muslims, Croats, and Serbs.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction. Political party, national political party needs to be included, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... of any national political party. Only the word national here is missing in line 19, page 32.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The interpreter has already corrected it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, would you agree with me - you indicated that certain political party programmes - did not suit you did the SDS policy of separation of the three ethnic groups, was that something that didn't suit you? Is that a policy that you --

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the SDS -- when the SDS advocated the use of force to separate the three ethnic groups, you weren't in favour of that either. Isn't that true, sir?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you aware that three of the main SDS leaders, Krajisnik, Karadzic, and Plavsic, have all been indicted as war criminals? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you aware that Biljana Plavsic, one of the former SDS leaders and a former Bosnian Serb leader has pled guilty and has admitted to a persecution campaign against the non-Serb population? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that she has admitted to implementing this policy objective of the ethnic separation by force, that she's admitted to that, that she as part of the SDS and Serb leadership has admitted to that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of that. What she admitted to and what she did, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have the break and continue our proceedings at 1100 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner. You can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning again, Mr. Vukovic. Sir, you, Simo Zaric, Miroslav Tadic, you three were not members of the SDS; correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to ask the Presiding Judge of the Trial Chamber for the Prosecutor not to ask me any other questions associated with political parties. I will not reply to such questions. I have not come here to respond to questions about politics but about the operation of the civil defence staff. Who was a member of what party is something that I was never concerned with. People followed their choices and their options and joined parties of their own volition. I wasn't interested in that at all. I cannot respond to such questions. Why Simo Zaric, why this or that person joined this or that party, I really was not interested in that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, you have come to the Tribunal as a witness in a criminal trial on an indictment referred by the Prosecution against these three accused persons. You have concluded your evidence-in-chief when you are answering questions by Mr. Lukic who called you on behalf of Mr. Tadic. According to our rules of evidence, the Prosecution, represented by Mr. Weiner who is now asking you questions, is entitled to ask you questions not only on the evidence in chief which you have given but also on any other matters which may support their case, the Prosecution case against the three accused persons. Such questions may include political activities of other people, including the accused persons. Your role, having made the solemn declaration, is to answer those questions as truthfully according to what you know. If any questions are not proper for you to answer, Mr. Lukic, as well as the Trial Chamber, will protect you by indicating to the Prosecutor that any such questions posed may not be answered by the witness. Where there is no such intervention, your obligation is to answer the question. If you don't know anything about the question posed, you say so, that you don't know. If you can't remember, you say so, that you can't remember. Mr. Weiner, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, let's move on for a few minutes to some other subject. Okay. We'll move on a little bit and then we'll get back to that, but let's just move on, okay? Yesterday you talked about Cafe AS. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was -- going there was one of your favourite places. Was that your favourite place to go before the war?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But this was in 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. In early -- before the war. 1991, early 1992.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as a frequent patron, you had a drink there, you'd play cards, you'd socialise, you had friends there; correct? Correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after the war began, you talked about going there and a couple of incidents that occur. You went there some time, I think in April or May you went there too.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I went there at that time but for short periods of time. I would not sit there and sit there for some time. I would just go there to attend to some business and then I would return to the staff where I worked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you went there, you talked about a couple incidents. You remember you talked about Avram who kind of got out of hand with a gun sometime while you were there in May?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you there for a while or did you leave immediately after that incident?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I could hardly wait to leave, to get myself away from that place. And it was not a pistol, it was an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, after that incident in May, did you again go to the Cafe AS in May or June, July? Did you go to the Cafe AS?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the last time you went was the time when Avram had the gun, in early May?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it so happened that I was there when two incidents took place. The first one with Ramusovic, and then this other one with Avram and Miroslav, and I didn't want to go there any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well -- so the place hadn't closed, you just decided not to go there any more after that, after the two incidents that had happened in May -- one in late April and one in early May?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just one quick question. When Avram was waving the gun, was he drinking? Had he had a few too many? Was he drunk or had --

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he certainly seemed drunk. And whether he had had a few too many or how much he had drunk, I don't know, but I was scared when he turned the gun towards me, where I was sitting, and Miroslav. It wasn't really pleasant. The only thing which I thought about was how to get away from the place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did he have any beer bottles in front of him or did you see any glasses, liquor glasses in front of him on that day? You said he sounded drunk or appeared drunk. Do you remember any beer bottles, or you just don't recall?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did any of your friends go to the Cafe AS after that incident? I know you didn't go, but did any of your friends go?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about these friends. Of these friends who went with me, they didn't go. And of other friends, when -- seeing that there was war and the conditions of war prevailed, I didn't actually see those other friends of mine, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So the last time that you went there was after this second violent incident was early May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the beginning of May. I don't know the exact date. I think it was the beginning of May, and I don't know the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, sir, being a Yugoslav, you don't believe in the persecution of any ethnic group, is that true? You, being a Yugoslav, don't believe in the persecution of any ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you didn't agree that non-Serbs should be deported from an area? You don't agree with that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't. Yes, I did not agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you did not agree that non-Serbs should be detained or imprisoned for no other reason than their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was always against it, irrespective of what ethnicity was in question or people being detained in prison, mistreated. Irrespective of their ethnicity, I always advocated such a view and will uphold it while I'm alive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's good. And you also didn't agree that non-Serb civilians should be forced to go to the front lines and dig trenches during the crossfire or during shelling. You don't agree with that either?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't agree with that, but that was war, the circumstances of war. Someone had to dig the trenches. The Serbs dug them. The Croats and Muslims dug trenches in the front line which was under the command of the Serb army, and the Serbs dug trenches where the territories of the Muslim and Croat armies were. That is how it is in war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you don't agree that someone should be forced to do that for no other reason than their ethnicity. You don't agree with that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I certainly do not agree, but as I said, this was a time of war, and the exigences of the circumstances of war is such that someone had to do it. All those Muslims and Croats who had chosen to take up arms and go and fight, they didn't dig trenches. Those who didn't choose to do that had to do this. Someone had to do it. And in conditions of war, it is the army that is making the decision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't take part in any of those actions, the deportations, forcing -- forcing people to dig trenches, the imprisonment of people? You didn't take part in any of those?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you didn't take part in evicting people or taking their houses strictly because of their ethnic backgrounds? You didn't take part in any of that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And isn't that the reason why you didn't join the SDS, because that's what the SDS was doing? Isn't that true, sir? You didn't like those SDS policies.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say whether the SDS did it when the war started. When the war started, all the parties got involved in the war, and irrespective of who belonged to what party, they had to get involved in the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But those SDS policies that I just mentioned of deportation which you've previously discussed, and detaining prisoners and taking houses, you didn't believe in any of those policies. That's why you later joined the SDP?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By choice, since I became of age was on the far left, and the politics of all other parties inclined towards the right was something which was not for me. We heard in Bosnia not only the SDP. We had the HDZ and the SDA. The same three parties but parties of different ethnicities, of different people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But strictly we're talking about the SDS. You didn't agree with those policies of the SDS that I've just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I must object, because my impression is that all this line of questioning are very confusing to this witness. In particular, I think the Prosecution should be more specific when he is make any reference to SDS. Time period, level of SDS, which kind of issues or policies so that this person, this witness, can be aware of the frame of the area of questions. Otherwise, it's too general, and it doesn't seem that it will be used as the evidence in these proceedings if we are following with these general terms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, your objection is not accepted, because the questions of the Prosecutor are quite specific, especially if you look at page 39, line 20. Mr. Weiner, please continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was: But those SDS policies of deportation, imprisonment based on ethnicity, taking of homes, forcing people to dig trenches during warfare on the front lines, you didn't agree with those SDS policies; correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Re-examination, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Re-examined by Mr. Lukic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Vukovic, good morning. The Prosecutor asked you whether in front of the pensioners' building you saw a large number of people going as part of a work detail on their assignments. I would like you to clarify for us the term the Prosecutor used, "A large number." What was the number that you saw assembling in front of the pensioners' house on the average to go to work?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you a precise number, but approximately, as far as I could see, conclude, there were between 40 and 50 people there who assembled there every morning and who would then be assigned to different work, not only in the town of Samac but also throughout the territory of Samac municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Prosecutor also asked you today about the repair of windows, the glazing work. Was any difference being made when it came to the glazing of windows in relation to the houses, whether the houses belonged to Muslims, Croats, or Serbs? Were all the windows glazed irrespective of the ethnicity of their owners?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, we had to glaze all the residential houses, the living quarters throughout the city of Samac irrespective of whether the owners were Croat, Serb, or Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Later when the nylons were being placed there were any differences being made between the different owners of the houses on that basis?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We in the civil defense staff made no distinction whatsoever between the citizens in Samac irrespective of what ethnic background they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Speaking on the subject you mentioned to the Prosecutor that the group, the work detail repairing these facilities, these buildings, was led by Ismet Ramusovic. You said yesterday but please repeat what you said now. What is he by ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that Ismet Ramusovic concretely led this particular group but he was greatly assisted by Trivo Lukic. These are two men in the civil defence staff who could do the -- such construction work and Ismet Ramusovic was a Muslim and Trivo Lukic a Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that they were knowledgeable in these but in that particular work, was that the reason why they were assigned to that particular job, their speciality?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We in the civil defence staff had agreed that each should do the work that he can do best.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The Prosecutor asked you a question in connection with the property of your family and the house. Yesterday you mentioned the name of Ibrahim Karic, a plumber who you said had worked in Samac throughout the war and who is still living in Samac today. Have you any information as to whether that man had ever been evicted from his house?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, which is to say I know that he had never been evicted from his house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the brothers Pistoljevic, Hasan and Mustafa.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. They're my neighbours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What are they by ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They're Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are they living in Samac today?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether their real property, their houses in which they live had ever been seized from them and has anyone lived in their houses apart from them?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. In fact, at the beginning of the war, Mustafa distributed milk and bread, drove it around the city of Samac and distributed it to the people there. He was working on that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was working for the Red Cross, was he not?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any other Muslims and Muslim families remain in your neighbourhood who never left their houses?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a family three houses down from my house, and there was another family five houses down from my house who remained there throughout that period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you perhaps know Ilija Ilic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is he by ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know -- are you aware of the fact that during the war this man left Samac?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you -- are you aware of the fact that third parties were moved into his apartment although it was a Serb apartment during the war?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object to that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: This isn't cross-examination. This is redirect. If you look at his last --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic, the objection is sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. I will rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you about Dusko Dragicevic. What is he by ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he in Samac during the war?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was there for a short time, then he fled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone move into his flat?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know Rade Radovanovic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is he by ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about his whereabouts and his property during the war?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about his movement, whereabouts during the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Prosecutor asked you towards the end of his questioning a few questions about the Cafe AS. Did you, before the war broke out, see any meetings held, any gatherings organised in the Cafe AS?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's outside the scope of cross-examination. I asked him about his attending the Cafe AS, being frequent before and after the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that catering establishments were prohibited to operate in the city of Samac for a while after the beginning of the war?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, that you have direct knowledge of the fact that the Cafe AS also was closed for a while, for a period?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know, but I don't know in which period.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's leading. He can ask when, but that's totally leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can rephrase your question, but it did arise in cross-examination, so -- it's just that it's a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Cafe AS work throughout the war, after the war conflict broke out?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Cafe AS did not work for a while, but for how long, for how many days, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
